answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when each useful island of identity must tie a refundable deposit to its reputation. An attacker who floods the network with fake agents must lock one bond per identity, so the horizon cost of a swarm scales linearly with every duplicate it spawns. Random audits check whether an agent performs its promised tasks; failing a check burns the bond and shares the stake among honest peers. This turns trust from a free registration into an oasis that only genuinely useful work can enter, making coordinated manipulation economically unprofitable.
